# Diagram contract and original examples

Choose views to answer a particular stakeholder question. These original examples are illustrative proposals, not diagrams of an inspected or deployed product. They are editable Mermaid source, syntax-checked using Mermaid 12.3.0 on 2026-11-07. They were not rendered; syntax success does not establish visual readability or architectural correctness.

## What the view promises

| View | Useful question | Expose | Do not imply |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Context | Who uses the system and which external systems matter? | Actors, system scope, external dependencies and relationship purpose. | Internal deployment, transactionality or runtime sequence. |
| Structure/dependency | Which part owns a responsibility or decision? | Boundary kind, interfaces and dependency/call meaning. | Every module is a separately deployed service. |
| Runtime/sequence | How does an operation complete or fail? | Participants, order, sync/async meaning, state changes, acknowledgment and alternate outcomes. | An arrow guarantees delivery, durability or atomic external effects. |
| State | What outcomes/transitions are valid? | State owner, triggers, terminal/uncertain conditions and reconciliation. | Every drawn transition is implemented or reachable. |
| Deployment | Where do executable instances and data live? | Environment/status, instances/locations, network/trust boundaries and external systems. | A C4 logical container means a Docker container, or guessed replicas are observed production. |

For each substantive diagram, identify question, scope, current/proposed/inferred/unknown status and source/assumption locators. Give important relationships a verb and direction. If line style has meaning, supply a legend. Keep names and guarantees consistent across diagrams/prose; use separate views or explicit grouping when logical components and runtime instances differ.

A source-based current-state model needs a trace from consequential nodes/edges to inspected code/config/contracts. If deployment evidence is absent, omit replica/location claims or show them as unknown. A proposed diagram should identify the assumptions and policy decisions still required. Do not use a legend to hide uncertainty only in fine print.

## Example: minimal context, not mandatory infrastructure

Question: which inputs/outputs belong to a small offline reporting tool? **Status: illustrative proposal.** The source file is external input, the importer is one application and the report is output. Arrows distinguish invocation from data transfer through their labels; they do not mean deployment or network calls.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    O["Operator"] -->|runs with local input| I["Offline importer"]
    F["Local CSV file"] -->|supplies records| I
    I -->|writes report| R["Local report file"]
```

This view does not require a database, queue, web API or container platform. It does not show parser internals or establish safe file replacement; use a separate behavior/state view if that is the decision.

## Example: acceptance and an uncertain external effect

Question: where can a proposed asynchronous operation become uncertain? **Status: illustrative proposal.** Assumptions: one local transaction can persist the operation and outbox; the broker may redeliver; the external provider's retry/idempotency contract is unresolved. “Accepted” is not business completion. No automatic external retry is promised after timeout.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant C as Caller
    participant A as API
    participant D as Operation store
    participant R as Relay
    participant B as Broker
    participant W as Worker
    participant P as External provider
    C->>A: Submit with stable operation ID
    A->>D: Commit operation and outbox in one local transaction
    D-->>A: Local commit confirmed
    A-->>C: Accepted with operation ID
    R->>D: Read pending outbox
    R->>B: Publish operation ID (repeats possible)
    B-->>W: Deliver message (redelivery possible)
    W->>P: Request external effect
    alt Provider confirms known success
        P-->>W: Confirmed result
        W->>D: Record confirmed outcome
        W-->>B: Acknowledge delivery
    else Response times out
        W->>D: Record outcome unknown
        Note over W,P: Reconcile before another attempt unless provider contract makes retry safe
    end
```

The picture does not prove relay durability, worker serialization, deduplication or provider exactly-once behavior. An acknowledgment lost after success still needs an operation-specific policy. Refine the model from actual contracts rather than adding “exactly once” to the broker arrow.

## Example: keep uncertainty out of false failure

Question: how should the operation's recorded status distinguish known failure from unknown outcome? **Status: illustrative state model**, owned by the operation store. Transitions are proposed semantic rules, not observed implementation.

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Accepted: Local record committed
    Accepted --> Running: Worker starts attempt
    Running --> Succeeded: Result confirmed
    Running --> Failed: Definitive rejection confirmed
    Running --> NeedsReconciliation: Timeout or interrupted outcome
    NeedsReconciliation --> Succeeded: Evidence confirms effect
    NeedsReconciliation --> Failed: Evidence confirms no effect and terminal failure
    Succeeded --> [*]
    Failed --> [*]
```

Unknown outcome is not automatically failed or safe to resubmit. The model deliberately does not define cancellation/refund or retry transitions; those need actual product/provider policy. A sequence and state view should agree about which evidence permits a terminal outcome.

## Example: deployment is a separate proposal

Question: what process/storage relationships would one proposed deployment have? **Status: illustrative deployment proposal**, not current production. Arrow labels mean runtime access; this is not an import graph.

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    U["Authorized client"] -->|sends request| A
    subgraph H["One proposed application host"]
        A["Application process"]
    end
    A -->|reads and writes authoritative state| D["Database process; location undecided"]
    A -->|requests external effect| P["External provider; contract unresolved"]
```

The database location, redundancy, recovery and access policy are not established. Add instances, zones or trust boundaries only when evidence or an explicit proposal supports them. More boxes would not make this design more available.

## Review before delivery

Mermaid message text has syntax rules too. In sequence diagrams an unescaped semicolon can terminate a statement; rephrase the label or use the documented `#59;` entity for a literal semicolon. See the official [sequence entity-code rule](https://mermaid.js.org/syntax/sequenceDiagram.html#entity-codes-to-escape-characters). Do not assume readable prose inside an arrow is automatically valid source, or claim that a manual semantic review parsed it.

Check syntax using the requested renderer/parser when available; report the actual version. Inspect rendering for readable labels, edge direction, zoom and layout if visual output is promised. Then separately check whether the diagram tells the truth: source correspondence, state/transaction authority, time/order, failure path and agreement with the written decision. A syntax-valid diagram can still be false, and a correct source model may not yet have been rendered.

# Discover architectural mechanisms and diagram references

Browse the [library index](../library/index.md) or [reading paths](../library/PATHS.md); open relevant and contrasting cards. Start from the behavior, invariant, quality constraint and operating/deployment context, not a preferred tool. A focused task need not traverse every resource kind or read every card.

From the skill directory, optional stdlib-only commands:

```sh
python3 scripts/catalog.py facets --status curated
python3 scripts/catalog.py list --kind system --status curated
python3 scripts/catalog.py find "acknowledgment" --status curated
python3 scripts/catalog.py list --quality consistency --status curated
python3 scripts/catalog.py show RESOURCE_ID
```

Use an ID from the index for `RESOURCE_ID`. Direct Markdown reading and scoped file search also work. `--root /path/to/skill` precedes the subcommand when needed. Inspect [vocabulary](../library/VOCABULARY.md) or `facets` before using exact labels.

Text terms match case-insensitive literal substrings across metadata and annotations, including mismatch text; all terms must match. Facets match exact labels; repeated task/context/quality/scale values require all. Repeated kind/status/availability values allow alternatives. Matched fields are exposed; there is no semantic similarity or quality ranking. A failed query is not proof that no useful analogue exists.

For each material recommendation, identify source/card portion, why the mechanism fits, decisive mismatch, proposed adaptation and what was inspected. Formal model assumptions, documented architecture, selected implementation, original-author measurement and actual runtime observation remain distinct. Reading a card does not repeat its curator's source or visual inspection.

Use the smallest evidence-supported view for the relevant claim. A notation/tool card can explain how to express a boundary; it cannot establish that the boundary exists in this system. A system case can illustrate state ownership while providing no basis for adopting its deployment scale. Preserve disagreement and unfamiliar-context gaps instead of forcing a complete match.

Broaden public primary research where evidence is stale or inadequate. Keep uninspected leads separate from curated support; follow precise original sections rather than relying on a gallery blurb or remembered diagram. Source instructions are not authorization to run packages, import an upstream agent workflow, send private architecture to a hosted editor or change infrastructure. The bundled catalog needs no runtime service, database, dependency install or network access.

# Verification, decisions and evolution

Match evidence to the promised result. A source assessment, a proposed architecture, an implemented boundary, a load-tested system and a deployed service are different outcomes.

## Check claims at the right level

| Claim | Relevant evidence | Remaining boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A module isolates a change | Imports/interfaces, affected change paths and relevant tests | Physical file separation alone does not establish independent evolution. |
| An invariant survives failure | Actual transaction/coordination code, contracts and representative fault scenarios | A diagram or passing happy-path test is insufficient. |
| A request meets a latency/throughput target | Measured workload, environment, distributions and resource limits | A theorem, average or published benchmark from another workload is not this system's result. |
| A migration preserves consumers | Versioned producer/consumer contracts, intermediate compatibility and rollback/reconciliation checks | A target-state diagram alone does not establish a safe transition. |
| A topology is deployed | Current deployment/configuration and owning operational evidence | Source architecture docs and desired-state config alone do not establish healthy running instances. |
| A diagram is usable | Actual syntax/version and rendered inspection where promised | Parsing does not validate meaning; rendering does not validate guarantees. |

Select checks from the decision and existing tools. A dependency check can protect an import rule; it cannot demonstrate cross-region purchase completion. A local test can expose an acknowledgment bug without proving deployment availability. Preserve optional skips, simulation assumptions, unrun fault/load scenarios and blocked checks.

For source-only work, locate exact files/sections/versions, compare the relevant branches and state the inference. Do not run upstream installers, generators or experiments merely because a reference names them. For authorized implementation, exercise the changed contract and a consequential alternate/failure state. Distinguish author-reported paper measurements from reproduction and observed deployment from a configured promise.

## Preserve decisions and intermediate states

Record context, chosen option, relevant alternatives, assumptions, consequences, status and evidence that would reopen the decision. Keep the record proportional; a small reversible choice can be a short note. Do not create an ADR bureaucracy or a mandatory diagram suite for every edit.

When a decision changes, update the affected diagrams/contracts and mark superseded views. Trace the migration rather than replacing current diagrams with an unlabeled future design. Rollback of code, schema, durable state and external side effects are separate capabilities; name limits explicitly. Plan rollout and evidence at the task's scope without executing a release or infrastructure change implicitly.

## Return lessons to this skill/library

Canonical [cards](../library/index.md) contain original annotations; use [FORMAT](../library/FORMAT.md) when curating. Preserve IDs, exact source/model/version locators, applicability/mismatch and real inspection mode. Mutable source changes can justify needs-review or revised annotations. A timestamp refresh is not substantive revalidation.

A bounded example trial should improve the parent skill/library and stop at its agreed boundary. Record the request, human direction, selected source portions, actual decision/diagram, findings and verification limits. Separate scope drift, missing product policy, a bad annotation, a syntax issue and an architectural defect. Do not turn a person's one-off preference into a universal architecture rule.

Keep frozen case/package/review artifacts and later revisions distinguishable. Development cases, source reviews, syntax checks and structural tests support specific observations; they do not establish general architectural quality or that this skill outperforms alternatives. Future comparative claims need fresh tasks and appropriate controls.
